newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks feature as Australian stocks close strongly.
newsitem.headline: Banks feature as Australian stocks close strongly.

text.p: SPI Futures 2393 +33 US 30yr cl 7.10 +0.03
10yrbond futs 91.985 -0.025 Gold NY 348.55 Lon fix 349.10
*Stocks extend gains in afternoon as interest returns, banks feature after Wallis report released. Volume 293.73 million, value A$869.05 million, 1,047 stocks traded, 328 steady, 393 up, 326 down.
The Australian share market locked in solid gains by the close on Wednesday as buyers returned to the market in numbers after the release of the Wallis report into the financial system.
By 4.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 20.3 points at 2,389.2. June share price index futures were up 33 points at 2,393, a 3.8 point premium to the index.

Predictably, banks featured in the day's trade with sharp share price movements in all the big four after the government said the ban on mergers between them would stay despite the removal of other restrictions, including foreign ownership.
"CommBank and NAB went ahead in leaps and bounds," said senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd, Jim Tredenick.

Commonwealth Bank shares climbed over two percent to A$12.98 while their instalment receipts soared over three percent to A$8.68. Sector leader National Australia Bank (NAB) added 2.5 percent to close at A$16.11 with brokers saying the Wallis report and the government's reactions had strengthened their positions.
However, previously mooted takeover targets Westpac Banking Corporation and ANZ Bank saw sharp dives as sellers squeezed takeover premiums out.
Westpac shares slid 2.9 percent to close at A$6.67, while ANZ Bank dived 3.6 percent to an intraday low of A$7.71 before bouncing back to close 1.4 percent lower at A$7.89.
News of the long-awaited report provided a release valve for some pent-up buying interest in a buoyant afternoon session, the most active seen so far this week.
"Costello's statement fuelled the banks and has dragged some of the market up with them," Tredenick said, noting that the long awaited report's release had helped investor interest.
"It has been a long drawn out affair but it has probably taken some uncertainty out of the market."

Other participants echoed similar sentiments, suggesting buying interest that would otherwise have been generated by the three consecutive stronger finishes in the U.S. had been delayed until the report saw the light of day.
"There were plenty holding off until the report came out, but now we've crossed that bridge they have come back to the market," said dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
Buying was concentrated among the leaders though, with buyers very picky about their purchases.
"It's all been very selective. BHP, WMC and the likes of Lend Lease and Brambles have seen good interest," he said.
Bellwether BHP added 14 cents to A$16.89 after touching the A$17.00 mark at its intraday peak while fellow miner WMC bounced 2.8 percent to close at A$7.82.

Keenly sought industrial blue chips included property and finance conglomerate Lend Lease Corporation, up 3.6 percent to A$22.532 while industrial services group Brambles Industries climbed 5.1 percent to A$21.60.
Topping turnover lists was Perth casino operator Burswood Property Trust after Tuesday's restructuring announcement. Its units jumped 21 cents to close at A$1.52 on turnover of 7.7 million units.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options markets were both active, reflecting the return of buying interest to the underlying markets in the afternoon session.
Total options traded 50,869 (43,138)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 9,633 (6,212)

In other local markets, Australian bonds closed slightly lower in line with some overnight weakness in U.S. Treasuries, but traders classed the day as consolidative and said the market still had a supportive tone after the rally of the past week.
By 5.30 p.m. (0710 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.99 percent, up on Tuesday's 7.96 percent.

The Australian dollar held onto 1/2 cent of offshore gains through a choppy session, breaking a four-day losing streak and establishing a short term uptrend for the recently beleagured currency. Traders said aggressive buying from a U.S. investment bank and hurried short covering had fuelled the rally which saw the unit hit US$0.7825 before attracting profit-taking.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT) the dollar had found a foothold at US$0.7810/15 from an early US$0.7805/10 and US$0.7772/77 late here Tuesday.
